name: Umai
hint: Sarawak Melanau raw fish ceviche, thin slices of fresh fish (tenggiri or terubok) tossed with lime, sliced shallot, chili and salt; very low calorie lean protein; variants udang (prawn), ikan tenggiri

name: Manok Pansoh
hint: Sarawak Iban/Bidayuh chicken cooked inside a bamboo tube with lemongrass, ginger, garlic and bungai kantan over fire; lean, broth-y, almost no added oil; one of the healthiest Borneo dishes; variants halia (ginger), cili

name: Midin
hint: Sarawak crunchy jungle fern (midin) stir-fried fast over high heat; very low calorie leafy veg, oil is the main calorie driver; variants belacan, garlic, masak lemak (with santan, higher)

name: Paku Pakis
hint: fiddlehead fern shoots (pucuk paku) stir-fried with belacan or sambal, common across Sabah/Sarawak/East Coast; low calorie veg, oil and any santan drive calories; variants belacan, goreng telur, masak lemak

name: Butod
hint: sago grub (sago worm) eaten in Sabah, raw and wriggling or skewered and grilled/fried; tourist novelty; high in fat for its size, coconut-creamy when raw, crispy when fried

name: Ikan Empurau
hint: prized expensive Sarawak river fish, usually steamed simply with ginger and soy to show off the fat from its wild diet of buah engkabang; lean-rich protein, premium dish

name: Kek Lapis Sarawak
hint: Sarawak layered cake, dense bands of butter-and-egg-rich batter baked layer by layer; extremely calorie dense from butter, condensed milk, eggs and sugar; many flavour variants (original/plain, chocolate, cheese, durian, gula apong, pandan) as rows ranked by calories

name: Khau Yuk
hint: Hakka braised pork belly with fermented bean curd or preserved mustard greens (mui choy) and sometimes yam, slow-braised until the fat is soft; very fatty, the pork belly is most of the calories

name: Abacus Seeds
hint: Hakka stir-fried yam-dough beads shaped like abacus seeds, chewy QQ texture, tossed with minced pork, dried shrimp, mushroom and black fungus; yam dough is the carb base, the toppings and oil add the rest

name: Ayam Masak Arak (Rice Wine Chicken)
hint: Foochow/Sarawak chicken braised in red glutinous rice wine (arak/ang chao) with ginger and sesame oil, a confinement dish from Sibu; sesame oil and wine sugars add calories

name: Butter Prawns
hint: prawns in a rich creamy butter sauce with curry leaves and egg-floss (nestum or egg strands); the butter, evaporated milk and oil make the sauce very calorie dense; salted-egg version similar

name: Chili Crab
hint: crab in a sweet, spicy, tomato-and-chili sauce thickened with egg, eaten with mantou or rice; the sugary starchy sauce is calorie dense, the crab meat itself is lean

name: Ikan Pari Bakar (Grilled Stingray)
hint: stingray wing grilled in banana leaf smothered in sambal belacan, hawker favourite; the fish is lean, the sambal oil and any extra sauce drive calories

name: Nasi Kukus
hint: steamed rice served with crispy spiced fried chicken (ayam goreng berempah) and sambal, a mamak and East Coast/Sabah favourite; the fried chicken and sambal drive calories, the steamed rice is plain

name: Daun Ubi Tumbuk
hint: pounded young cassava leaves cooked with coconut milk, lemongrass and sometimes salted fish or ikan bilis, popular in Sarawak/Sabah; fibrous greens, the santan adds the calories

name: Wild Boar (Babi Hutan)
hint: wild boar meat, leaner and gamier than farmed pork, eaten in Sabah/Sarawak; variants curry, stir-fry with bamboo shoot, smoked; non-halal; fat content depends a lot on the cut and cooking

name: Sago Gula Melaka
hint: chilled sago pearl pudding drenched in palm sugar (gula melaka) syrup and coconut milk; the gula melaka syrup and santan are most of the calories, the sago is light

name: Tenom Coffee
hint: Sabah Tenom wok-roasted robusta coffee (Yit Foh), strong and aromatic; variants kopi O (black, near zero), kopi C (with evaporated milk), white coffee with condensed milk; milk and sugar drive calories

name: Air Barli
hint: barley drink, boiled pearl barley sweetened with sugar and often rock sugar, sometimes with lemon (barli limau); the added sugar is most of the calories, the barley is minimal

name: Coffee Bun (Rotiboy)
hint: Rotiboy-style soft bun with a butter core and a baked-on crisp coffee-cream topping; the butter filling and sweet topping make it surprisingly calorie dense for its size
